subject: Follow-up: Model fit evals & tool-calling schema checks
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: model fit & tool-calling needs

Thanks again for the demo today — that was super helpful. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can move to a scoped eval: 

Goal: integrate Redwood-hosted inference to produce structured transaction classification outputs via function-calling (JSON schema). Must be high-fidelity (strict schema compliance) because this feeds downstream accounting systems.

Traffic/SLAs: target ~200 req/s at peak, p95 latency <= 250ms, cost-sensitive but accuracy-critical.

Key questions / asks:
- Recommended model(s) for initial eval (balance cost + structured-output robustness).
- Any benchmark links or prior evals (tool-calling / structured output) we can review.
- Prompt sets / example payloads we should run (we can share a sanitized sample dataset).
- How Redwood handles schema validation failures and retry semantics (should retries be automated? how many attempts?).
- Concern: we need to detect quality regressions quickly — what monitoring / eval cadence do you recommend?

Next steps we want from you: short written plan that includes recommended models, eval plan (sample size), expected pass thresholds for schema compliance, and suggested retry/backoff policy. Also let us know what access you need (sample data, API keys or temp creds).

Thanks,
Samir
Senior Product Manager, FinTechCo

--
External: FinTechCo is evaluating multiple inference vendors; this thread may be shared internally with procurement.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & tool-calling schema checks

Thanks Samir — great meeting. Below is a concise plan and recommendations we can act on immediately. I copied Rishi for the technical runbook.

High-level recommendations (initial eval):
- Recommended models: redwood-open-7b (fast, cost-effective) and redwood-13b-q4 (higher quality, quantized for cost savings). For embeddings-based retrieval/validation, use redwood-embed-2-small.
- Quantization suggestion: test q4 variants for 13b to reduce cost while preserving structured-output fidelity.

Benchmark links & collateral:
- Redwood structured-output evals & prior tool-calling benchmarks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-benchmarks
- Eval harness (example configs): https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/tree/fintechco

Suggested eval plan (we can run this for you):
- Sample size: 1,000 unique prompts drawn from your sanitized dataset (we recommend stratifying by transaction type).
- Metrics: 
  - Schema compliance rate (JSON schema validation pass) — target >= 98%
  - Business-logic accuracy (classification labels) — target >= 95%
  - Structured key fidelity (types, optional/required keys) — target >= 99%
  - Latency/p95 under target load profile (we'll simulate 200 req/s)

Structured-output checks & retries:
- Parser-first approach: run JSON schema validation on the model output. If validation fails due to parse errors (unclosed JSON, trailing text), attempt a single automatic reformat/retry with a corrected prompt (server-side) — max 1 auto-retry with 250ms backoff.
- If retry still fails, escalate to the fallback policy:
  1) Run the same prompt on redwood-open-7b for comparison (faster, sometimes more deterministic output).
  2) If both fail, mark for human review and surface in the error dashboard with the raw outputs.
- Idempotency: include a request_id in calls to ensure retries are safe on your side.

Quality regression monitoring:
- We'll provide a daily regression score for the evaluated prompt set for the first 14 days, then weekly thereafter.
- Alerts if schema compliance drops > 1% or business-logic accuracy drops > 2% vs baseline.

Attachments & artifacts we can deliver now:
- Prompt sets (sanitized examples) — attaching: avery_prompt_sets_v1.zip
- JSON schema templates and examples: schema_templates.json
- Eval matrix & runbook we will use: eval_matrix.csv, runbook.md

Operational notes / access required:
- Please upload a sanitized sample of ~1,000 prompts (S3 or shared Drive) and a small schema file if you have a preferred format.
- Temporary API key for Redwood staging project (we can also run entirely on our side if you prefer).

Proposed timeline:
- Kickoff: once we have sanitized data and your approval, we can start within 2 business days.
- Delivery: initial report with pass/fail matrix and recommended model variant in 7 business days from start.

If that plan looks good I can get Rishi to spin up the harness and start the run. Can we schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to confirm dataset and access?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & tool-calling schema checks

Hi Samir — thanks, and happy to run the eval when you give the green light. A few technical clarifications and what we'll execute: 

Execution plan (technical):
- Harness: we'll use the finch eval harness (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/tree/fintechco). We'll containerize the run and provide the raw output CSV and JSONL.
- Baselines: redwood-open-7b and redwood-13b-q4; we'll record raw model outputs, parse attempts, and final normalized JSON.
- Schema validation: we will run ajv-based JSON schema validation (strict mode). For parse failures we will attempt a lightweight canonicalization pass (strip leading text, fix trailing commas) and re-run validation once.

Retry & idempotency details:
- Auto-retry: max 1 automated retry triggered only on parse/validation errors (not on incorrect business labels). Backoff: 250ms.
- Manual / programmatic fallback: if auto-retry fails, invoke the 7b variant as a fallback. We'll tag fallback results in the output (fallback=true).
- Attempts metadata: every call will return attempt_count and request_id in logs to help you reconcile downstream systems.

Metrics & pass criteria:
- Schema pass rate (ajv strict): pass if >= 0.98 on the 1k sample.
- Business accuracy: we'll compute micro/macro F1 vs your ground truth. Target > 0.95 but we'll surface confusion matrices so we can iterate.
- Parsing error rate: target < 1% after retries.

What we need from you to start:
- Sanitized prompt set (1k) and the authoritative JSON schema (or tell us which of our templates to use).
- Temporary staging API key OR permission for us to run the eval on Redwood-hosted staging under your account.
- A primary contact for data questions (name/email) — we'll assume Samir unless you prefer otherwise.

Deliverables:
- Raw outputs (JSONL), eval summary, recommended model variant, suggested prompt engineering tweaks, and a short runbook for production integration. We'll attach eval_matrix.csv and runbook.md as part of the deliverable.
- Target delivery: 7 business days from kickoff (target date: 2027-05-07 if we start on 2027-04-29).

I'll start prepping the harness today — Marissa, I'll ping you once the container is ready. Samir, once you upload the sanitized prompts to the shared Drive link above (or give us API access), we'll begin.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Applied ML / Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
